title: 2025 Hubbard Glacier earthquake — Mount King George radar surface change
location: Mount King George, Kluane region, Yukon, Canada
summary: Real Sentinel-1A images show surface-backscatter change around Mount King George following the December 2025 Hubbard Glacier earthquake. Coherent increases are visible on accepted low-slope glacier/deposit support; snowfall, wetness and glacier dynamics remain competing causes. No landslide or damage area is classified.

methods.title: Same-platform satellite change
methods.description: Sentinel-1A VV/VH, ascending relative orbit 50; exact UTC acquisitions 16 November control, 28 November baseline and 10 December comparison. Mean native linear power on the anchored 30 m UTM grid, then convert to dB. Signed difference is comparison minus baseline. This is amplitude analysis, not InSAR or displacement.

methods.title: Conservative deposit-observation support
methods.description: Require complete VV/VH native support, incidence 30–45°, pairwise mean-angle difference ≤0.5°, and GLO30 slope ≤20°. Common and control eligible coverage gates pass; full-box coverage remains 66.04%. Low slopes and close angles do not establish complete local/distant shadow or layover freedom. No radiometric terrain flattening is claimed.

methods.title: Control, ambiguity and display limits
methods.description: Inspect the earlier 12-day repeat alongside event differences. Both contain positive regional background change; coherent event patches alone do not prove pixel-level attribution. Snow, ice, moisture and glacier movement remain confounders. ±7 dB display clipping affects strong patches while numerical rasters preserve the range.

methods.title: Frozen export and independent audit
methods.description: Original Colab selection, numerical manifest, processing receipt and provider audit remain byte-identical with unapproved history. Independent local checks rerun full numerical TIFFs. The portable source package retains those inputs; the website ships durable PNGs and hashed records. No credentials or live Earth Engine tile URLs are used.

limitations: Exploratory satellite observations, not independently validated damage, an official affected-area total or an emergency warning. Blank/excluded pixels are unknown, not unchanged.

Accepted common observations cover 66.04% of the full box (298.78 km²), despite 100% coverage of the deliberately low-slope eligible support. The remaining terrain is excluded/unknown; no complete earthquake footprint is claimed.

Earlier repeat medians are already positive: VV +1.19 dB and VH +1.29 dB, versus event-interval +2.24/+2.65 dB. Equal 12-day timing does not make this a calibrated counterfactual or significance test.
Difference colours saturate beyond ±7 dB: 11.59% of accepted VV and 15.04% of VH samples exceed +7 dB. Full numerical values are retained; saturation is not a landslide threshold.
This is measured radar-amplitude/backscatter change, not InSAR displacement, earthquake shaking, confirmed landslides, building damage or losses. GRD contains no phase information for interferometry.
Snowfall, wetness, melt/freeze, glacier motion and viewing/processing effects can change backscatter. Timing and documented regional landslides do not establish the cause of every changed pixel.

Only low-slope support (Copernicus GLO30 slope ≤20°) with matched same-platform ascending orbit, accepted incidence angles and complete source support is admitted. This omits steep landslide source/transport areas and is not a complete event footprint.

Earth Engine terrain-corrects Sentinel-1 GRD geometrically but does not perform radiometric terrain flattening. The low-slope and angle screens reduce some problems; they do not prove freedom from local/distant terrain shadow, layover or foreshortening.

C-band radar responds to surface properties. Positive VV change can be consistent with rougher avalanche deposits on glaciers, but cannot uniquely distinguish rock, snow, ice or other causes. No damage or landslide area is reported.

Each period is one exact frame/date. Three-by-three approximate native-sample power aggregation to a 30 m lattice reduces speckle but does not remove it or create independent observations. Continuous differences and a pre-event repeat must be visually reviewed.

No-data and excluded steep terrain are unknown, not unchanged. A successful coverage gate applies only to the explicitly low-slope eligible denominator; the full domain coverage is reported separately.

The USGS provisional SAR/landslide products used the same acquisitions and are contextual corroboration, not an independent pixel-level accuracy reference. The EE preprocessing and conservative support differ from the USGS product.
